I’m extremely disappointed with the quality and thoroughness of the home inspection I received.

I hired Dylan. This was a new-construction home, and I hired an inspector specifically to identify defects while I still had the opportunity to get them addressed by the builder. The initial inspection identified only a small number of issues, including some stucco cracking, a garage door spring problem, and a low HVAC temperature differential.

At my one-year warranty inspection, a different inspector identified a much broader list of concerns involving major systems and construction workmanship, including roofing defects, visible roof sagging/waviness, attic insulation deficiencies, damaged and poorly installed HVAC ductwork, electrical panel concerns, loose receptacles, plumbing and water-heater safety issues, widespread stucco defects, and other deficiencies.

What concerns me most is that several of these conditions appear related to original construction or installation—not ordinary wear and tear—and some involve systems that should have been visually evaluated during the first inspection.

One example is the stucco. The original report described cracking as “typical for a newer home” and recommended sealing it as normal maintenance. The one-year inspection documented a much broader range of stucco concerns, including excessive cracking, voids/openings, exposed lath, loose or improperly finished areas, and bulging/bowing. That is a very different level of concern.

The original inspector did correctly identify the low HVAC cooling differential and garage door spring issue, and I want to be fair about that. However, given the number and nature of the additional construction-related conditions identified later, I have serious concerns about how thorough the original inspection was.

A new-home inspection is especially important because the homeowner has a limited window to identify construction defects and pursue builder warranty repairs. I relied on this inspection for exactly that purpose. Discovering this many additional issues at the one-year inspection has left me questioning how many opportunities for early correction may have been lost.

Based on my experience, I would strongly recommend that anyone considering this inspector carefully review the scope of the inspection, ask how thoroughly the roof, attic, electrical panel, plumbing, HVAC distribution, and other major systems will be examined, and consider obtaining a second opinion before important builder warranty deadlines expire. No wonder he’s on the builders “Pre approved inspector” list. I’ll be sure to add proof of services since this company likes to scoff off complaints as unverified customers.

Extremely disappointing experience and unacceptable customer service
I rarely write reviews—in fact, I have never posted a Google review, good or bad—but my experience with Auto Glass Now was disappointing enough that I felt it was important to share.
I made an appointment to replace the cracked windshield on my 2020 Volvo XC90. I dropped off the vehicle, and about 30 minutes later I received a text saying they could not replace the windshield because the vehicle's computer was showing error codes.
Ryan, who was working at the front desk, recommended that I take the vehicle to a calibration specialist to have the codes addressed. I followed his recommendation. The specialist cleared some old codes and found one remaining code that he wanted to investigate further. According to him, that code was unrelated to the windshield camera or the windshield replacement. Importantly, the specialist personally called Ryan and told him that they could proceed with the windshield replacement.
By then, however, I was told I needed to reschedule.
I made another appointment for the next available date, brought the vehicle back, and left it with them again. About 30 minutes later, I received another text saying they could not perform the replacement because there were error codes in the computer.
Naturally, I was confused. I asked for a supervisor to call me, but no one ever did.
When I returned to pick up the vehicle, I asked Ryan what had happened, particularly since he had already spoken directly with the calibration specialist who had told him they could proceed. Instead of simply explaining the situation, Ryan responded in an incredibly condescending manner:
"Well, sir, how many calibrations have you done in your life? None, I believe. We have performed thousands here, and I can tell you we cannot touch that car. I don't tell you how to run your business."
I was stunned by the response. I remained calm and told him that, at that point, I definitely would not have the windshield replaced there, but I still wanted to understand what had changed and why they had scheduled me for a second appointment if they were not prepared to perform the work.
His response was essentially, "Well, sir, there is no point for me to continue this conversation," and he dismissed me.
The technical issue is not why I am writing this review. If Auto Glass Now did not feel comfortable working on my vehicle, that is their right. My issue is the way I was treated after following their instructions, taking my vehicle to the specialist they recommended, returning for a second appointment, and simply asking for an explanation.
There was absolutely no reason for an employee to speak to a customer in such a condescending and dismissive way.
What bothered me even more was that I left the interaction with the uncomfortable feeling that my strong Mexican accent may have influenced the way I was being treated. I cannot know whether that was the case, but I can say that I felt disrespected and unwelcome.
I have been a customer of many businesses over the years and have never felt compelled to write a negative Google review until now. Customers deserve to be treated with basic courtesy and respect, even when a business decides it cannot perform the requested work.
Unfortunately, that was not my experience at Auto Glass Now.

one_star_reviews.text:
Our experience with RPM Living following move-out has been extremely frustrating and disappointing.

RPM Living took over management of my daughter's apartment community, The Pointe at South Mountain in Phoenix, during our tenancy. After moving out, we received a Final Account Statement containing $815 in additional charges for carpet repair/cleaning, painting/touch-up, housekeeping, and vinyl flooring repair. We had a $600 security deposit on the account.

We disputed the additional move-out charges in writing on July 15 and requested supporting documentation, including the move-in inspection checklist, move-out inspection report, photographs of the alleged damage, and invoices/work orders supporting the charges.

We received no response.

We followed up again by email on August 3. Again, no response.

I called the property on August 6 in an attempt to speak with someone about the dispute and was told there was nobody available who could assist me.

Despite never responding to our written dispute or providing any of the documentation we requested, the account was subsequently referred to a collection agency. Both my daughter and I have now been contacted regarding the alleged balance.

We have photographs documenting the condition of the apartment after it was completely emptied and cleaned, and we have maintained copies of our correspondence and attempts to resolve this matter.

At this point, we have sent formal correspondence by certified mail to the property and RPM Living management and have separately disputed the collection account in writing.

I understand that move-out charges can sometimes be legitimate. My concern is not simply that we were charged. My concern is that we promptly disputed specific charges, requested the documentation supporting them, made repeated attempts to communicate, and received no substantive response before the account was sent to collections.

I am posting this review because communication and responsiveness are extremely important when a company is handling residents' security deposits and potentially affecting their credit. I will gladly update this review if RPM Living responds, provides the requested documentation, and works with us in good faith to resolve the dispute.

Update 8/13/26: RPM Living responded publicly to this review and stated that they are “eager to offer insight and ensure [we] feel heard.” I appreciate the acknowledgment. The Pointe at South Mountain also received our formal dispute by certified mail today. As of this update, however, we have not received any direct communication addressing the disputed charges or any of the documentation we have repeatedly requested. I will continue to update this review if/when RPM Living substantively responds and works with us toward a resolution.

Patient abandoned after DBS surgery – denied a second opinion.
I am writing this out of sheer frustration and disappointment with the care—or lack thereof—I have received at Barrow Neurological Institute. Two years ago, I underwent invasive Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) surgery here to treat my essential tremor. Not only has my tremor failed to improve, but it is now equal to or worse than it was before the operation. Worse yet, the side effects from the current DBS stimulation settings are entirely debilitating. I am currently suffering from severely slurred speech, major balance issues, and a gait that makes me walk as if I am heavily intoxicated. I have been tracking these issues with my current neurologist at Barrow for the last year and a half with zero successful results. It has now been nearly three months since my neurologist last saw me. She is fully aware that my tremor is severe and that my device desperately requires programming adjustments to mitigate these awful side effects, yet I have been left waiting. When I proactively advocated for my own health and requested a second opinion from a different doctor within Barrow's movement disorder group, my request was flatly rejected. Barrow Neurological Institute has completely given up on me as a patient. They are content leaving me with life-altering side effects from a brain surgery they performed, while actively blocking me from seeking internal expertise. If you expect continuous, compassionate follow-up care and a team that won't abandon you when a procedure doesn't go perfectly, look elsewhere.

Yes, I wanted to purchase a car so we visited Charlie at Bill Luke auto center. We found a car that we liked only to find out that that car had a branded car title  and if you don’t know what a branded car title is, it is  a salvage vehicle we questioned this information with the sales manager. Both the salesman and the sales manager told us that all their customers have had zero problem getting these branded  salvage title cars  insured . Well we decided that we would contact our insurance agent since they are a major insurer, as well as additional research to other insurance companies. We learned that yes these cars can be insured however, what they don’t tell you at Bill Luke, that our insurance agent  told u, is that due to being a salvage title if they were to have to do a claim for any reason on that vehicle, they would only cover it for 75% max of the cars value at the time. With that information we noted the car was $3000 above that 75%, so we called down and spoke to the sales manager, asking him if he would be willing to go down by a few thousand dollars, so that we wouldn’t be upside down on the car from the time of purchase.  His statement was nope not gonna do it. I will not go down that far on that car,  basically he didn’t want to sell us the car for fair market value. My complaint is that he was extremely rude.  So please people you do not want to buy a branded car from Bill Luke or anyone who sells them above value. If you do, you will be upside down and if you get in an accident and your $50,000 car is only worth 32 or 33,000 and all of a sudden you have to go buy a cheap car to replace the beautiful car you thought you purchased fairly, additionally, on the insurance part when you go to insure  the car they’re going to charge you premiums at the rate that the car would be worth as if it was not a branded title or salvage title so you’ll pay premiums on that big beautiful $50,000 car but you will not ever be covered to replace a $50,000 car or whatever your price point difference is. So a branded title is none other than a salvage title a very important thing to know check with your insurance companies they will tell you if they will cover it and what they will cover it for, at Bill, Luke Sales manager and Sales team will absolutely tell you that they have no problem with their customers getting insured that actually is a true statement if you’re willing to overpay for a car and be under insured for that car.Buyer beware.

I strongly recommend that anyone considering doing business with this company research customer complaints and carefully read and keep copies of every document before providing personal or company information.

Updated Review — August 25, 2026

A couple of weeks ago, I left a review about our experience with RGroup, something I honestly did not want to do. I don't enjoy publicly criticizing businesses, but at that point, I felt like RGroup had left us with no other choice. After leaving the review, I genuinely felt like maybe we had finally been heard. Unfortunately, that feeling didn't last long.

Since then, there has been no meaningful contact from management. I have called several times and have not received a return call. I have also tried to find an email address for someone in management so that we can communicate directly, but that has been extremely difficult.

To put our situation into perspective: we have now been dealing with an on-and-off leak for over a year. What was once an intermittent issue has now become a consistent drip of brown water coming from the ceiling of the bathroom our children use. The ceiling is visibly damaged and appears to have mold, and the damage has now begun spreading into the dining room ceiling.

Since the beginning of June, we have literally had to go into the bathroom every day and empty a bucket collecting water from the ceiling.

Unfortunately, the concerns with the property don't stop there. The roof of the house has sustained significant damage from recent storms, and to our knowledge, there is still no clear plan or timeline for getting the roof properly repaired. This is extremely concerning because the ongoing roof issues may be contributing to the water damage we are already experiencing inside the home. We have repeatedly tried to get answers, yet we still don't have a clear understanding of when this will actually be resolved.

We have been RGroup customers for approximately four years and have always paid our rent on time. We have continued doing our part as tenants and paying full rent even while being unable to fully use part of our home.

That is what makes this situation so disappointing.

For months, all we wanted was for the problem to be properly addressed and repaired. Instead, we have received promises that repeatedly haven't been followed through on, conflicting information, and what feels like an endless runaround.

At this point, the lack of communication and follow-through has left us feeling that these issues are simply not being treated with the urgency they deserve.

We are talking about my wife, my children, and me living in a home with an ongoing water leak, damaged ceilings, apparent mold, and significant unresolved roof damage. This is no longer just an inconvenience. It is a serious issue involving the condition and sanitation of our home.

And now, after paying full rent for a home that we have not had 100% use of for months, we are asking for more than just the repairs. We believe a fair rent credit is appropriate for the portion of our home that has been unusable while these issues have remained unresolved.

We have tried to be patient. We have tried to communicate. We have continued paying our rent. We have given RGroup numerous opportunities to make this right.

Unfortunately, our trust in RGroup has been seriously damaged.

I am genuinely disappointed and saddened that a company we have rented from for four years would allow major issues like this to continue for so long.

We don't want conflict. We want our home repaired, our family to have a safe and sanitary living environment, and to be treated fairly for the time we've been paying full rent without full use of our home.

That shouldn't be too much to ask.

We have rented through RGroup for five years, and up until this point, we have had a good experience. Unfortunately, our experience over the past year has been extremely disappointing.

We have been dealing with a recurring ceiling leak in our guest bathroom since August 2025. What started as an occasional leak has now become a fast, persistent drip, and we have essentially been without use of the bathroom for the entire summer. The ceiling damage is now noticeable and appears to be spreading into the dining room as well.

I have contacted RGroup’s maintenance department at least 20–30 times regarding this issue. We have repeatedly been told that the necessary work was approved, only to later be told that it was no longer approved or that they were still waiting for the owner to respond. This has happened multiple times, and the work still has not been completed.

HVAC has also been out to the house repeatedly and has told us that this is not an HVAC issue.

The most frustrating part is continuing to be told that the owner simply will not respond. We have been responsible tenants for five years, have consistently paid 100% of our rent on time, and have always done our part as renters. Yet we have not had 100% access to the home we are paying for.

The bathroom is located next to our children’s room, and naturally, we are concerned about the ongoing moisture, potential mold, and other issues that can come from leaving a leak unresolved for this long.

We have been incredibly patient throughout this process. We did not want to leave a negative review because that is not really who we are. But after dealing with this since August 2025, we are hoping that bringing this situation to light will finally get someone’s attention.

At this point, we simply want RGroup to step up, take responsibility, properly repair the ceiling and underlying issue, and consider providing a reasonable credit for the extended period in which we have not had full use of our home.

We have been loyal tenants, we have held up our end of the bargain, and we simply want the same consideration in return. We truly hope RGroup does the right thing and helps resolve this.

Super disappointed we are approaching over a year that’s we’ve been dealing with this issue. It’s laughable that a company can be this blatant ignoring their responsibilities. Three sets of tires in 26 months. I've paid this service center $2,955.24 for tires alone, plus another set out of pocket at Discount Tire, and I'm about to need a fourth.

In between, this car needed two front left hub assemblies in 14 months, a halfshaft, and a control arm with a torn bushing. Every complaint got dismissed before it got confirmed. The front-end noise I reported on delivery day was a normal characteristic of the vehicle, until it was a failing hub. The steering shake I reported two weeks after a fresh alignment was no sign of alignment issue during test drive, four months before they found the loose fasteners. ⭐ 1 Star — Very Disappointing Experience

I am extremely disappointed with my experience with this location.

In mid-June, I met with Julie, the location attendant, because I was looking for a business address. We initially discussed an office for approximately $140 per month. During the conversation, I explained that I did not actually need office space — what I really needed was a business address.

Julie told me they had another option for approximately $60–$70 per month that would provide the address service I needed. I told her that this option sounded good to me.

She asked me to provide my information and fill out a form. At the end of the meeting, she told me their system was not working and that she would send me the agreement the next day so I could review and sign it.

I never received that agreement.

I never returned to use the office, never used the office space, and never understood that I had entered into an office rental agreement.

Then, at the beginning of August, I suddenly received an invoice for more than $600.

I was shocked.

I immediately started contacting customer support and trying to reach Julie. I have been transferred between different departments and have had an extremely difficult time getting anyone to actually resolve the issue.

I have also escalated the matter to regional management, including Donna Sherro, and I am still trying to get these charges removed.

After this happened, I also checked the company’s BBB profile and found other customer complaints describing similar types of billing and cancellation issues. I strongly recommend that anyone considering doing business with this company research customer complaints and carefully read and keep copies of every document before providing personal or company information.

Based on my experience, I cannot recommend this company.

I am disputing the entire amount and have requested that the company provide me with a complete copy of any agreement they claim I accepted, including the pricing, terms, and evidence showing when and how I accepted it.

I hope management resolves this issue and removes the disputed charges. If they do, I will be happy to update my review to reflect the resolution.

For now, based on my personal experience, this is a 1-star review.

I have trusted Phoenix Children’s with my kids for nearly 17 years, which is exactly why this experience was so disappointing.

I brought my son in because he needed minor medical attention that could not wait until morning, and Phoenix Children’s was the only nearby facility open. Based on our previous experiences with PCH, I didn’t think twice about bringing him there.

While we waited, our insurance information was taken. I specifically told the person collecting our information that I could not find the correct address in their system that matched the address on our insurance card. At no point were we told that our insurance was not accepted or that there was an issue processing it. Had we been told that, we could have made an informed decision about whether to continue with treatment or go elsewhere.

Instead, the first indication we had that there was a problem was when the bills started arriving. We are now receiving multiple bills totaling approximately $5,000 for this single visit, including separate facility, provider, and testing charges.

What makes this even more frustrating is the level of care involved. The visit consisted primarily of a roughly five-minute ultrasound and an extremely brief interaction with the provider. I also question why the ultrasound was performed before we had a meaningful evaluation by the provider to determine whether it was actually necessary.

Had we been able to use an urgent care that evening, the same type of visit likely would have cost us under $500. Instead, we are being charged thousands.

Since receiving the bills, I have called PCH multiple times trying to resolve this. Our account was supposedly “reviewed,” but from my experience, that amounted to postponing payment rather than actually investigating or addressing our concerns. Even more frustrating, when our insurance requested that PCH complete a single form so the claim could potentially be addressed, PCH billing refused to complete it.

My biggest issues are simple:

1. We provided our insurance information before treatment and specifically raised a concern about the information in their system, yet no one informed us that our insurance was not accepted.
2. We were not given the opportunity to make an informed financial decision before thousands of dollars in charges were incurred.
3. Testing was performed without what I felt was an adequate provider evaluation beforehand to determine whether it was necessary.
4. After the fact, we actively tried to work with both PCH and our insurance company, yet PCH would not even complete the requested form that could potentially help resolve the claim.

I understand that medical care costs money, and I am not asking to receive care for free. What I expect is transparency, reasonable communication, and some willingness to help when a billing issue arises.

After nearly 17 years of mostly positive experiences with Phoenix Children’s, this visit has significantly changed my opinion. Right now, it feels far more focused on collecting payment than helping a longtime patient family resolve a legitimate billing concern.

Very disappointed.

Maintenance was also inconsistent. Our ice machine stopped working, was fixed, and then broke again. There were also damages/issues already present when we moved in.

I contacted this company for an estimate on a full exterior painting project. From the beginning, I was told how much they value their customers—especially military families—and that they would do whatever was necessary to make their customers feel valued and taken care of.

Unfortunately, our experience did not reflect those promises.

After our initial conversation, I was told I would receive a follow-up to schedule the estimate. When that never happened, I reached out myself. We eventually scheduled a time, only to have communication issues and delays again. After rescheduling, I was informed he was running late. At that point, I made it clear that my confidence was declining because this was already the second time our schedule had been disrupted.

Despite that, I was willing to rearrange my schedule a third time and give the company another opportunity.

Then, after we had once again made arrangements around the agreed-upon appointment, I received a message stating that he did not feel he was the right contractor for our project and did not want to work with us.

The most frustrating part isn't that they declined the project. Contractors have every right to decide which jobs they take. It's the complete disregard for our time and the repeated inconvenience after we had been more than patient and accommodating with theirs.

My husband, my children, and I all had to rearrange our schedules multiple times for an appointment that ultimately never happened. Our time is just as valuable as theirs, and we expected the same consideration and professionalism that we extended to them.

It's especially disappointing to repeatedly hear how much a company "takes care of military families" and makes customers feel valued, only to experience the exact opposite.

Communication, reliability, and respect for a customer's time cost nothing. Unfortunately, that's what was missing here.

I sincerely hope other customers have a better experience, but based on ours, I would not recommend this company.

​Location: Take 5 Oil Change (Cave Creek & Thunderbird Rd)
​If you value your vehicle, your safety, and your hard-earned money, stay as far away from this shop as possible.
​I brought my truck into this location for a routine oil service—a routine service this vehicle has received here multiple times without issue. This time, their technician failed to perform the most basic step of an oil change: they failed to properly tighten the new oil filter.
​Because the technician left the filter loose, 4 quarts of oil leaked out between the filter and the engine block in under 10 miles. Out of a total 5.3-quart capacity, the engine was left running on roughly 1.3 quarts of oil. This acute oil starvation resulted in a catastrophic, total engine failure.
​Instead of taking accountability for an open-and-shut mistake, Take 5, its corporate office, and its claims division have engaged in endless stonewalling:

At first, I did not want to write this review because I was emotionally exhausted after learning that my son has leukemia. But I am writing it now because hospital administration needs to pay closer attention to how some front desk employees treat parents of seriously ill children.
This happened on June 11 at approximately 5:00 p.m. Please review your security camera footage.
This was far from my first visit to this hospital. My oldest son had surgery here in 2016. My middle son was treated here in 2021 after suffering a stroke, and we have continued coming here for neurology appointments. I have also brought my daughter here for orthopedic care.
On June 10, I came with my children to visit my son on the 7th floor after chemotherapy. I told the front desk I was his mother. They gave me a “Visitor” sticker and allowed us upstairs without any issue.
The next day, June 11, I returned around 5:00 p.m. with my 5-month-old baby, my 10-year-old son, and three heavy bags. The reception area was nearly empty. The receptionist asked whether I was my son’s biological mother, and when I said yes, she told me I now needed a wristband.
I explained that the day before I had been given a Visitor sticker. I was not refusing the wristband — I simply wanted to understand why the rules were different. Instead of explaining, I was sent to another window #1.
At the wristband window, the employee held my government-issued ID while repeatedly asking for my name, last name, date of birth, and asking me to spell my name multiple times. I answered, but after being asked again and again, I told her I was exhausted and asked her to please look at the ID already in her hand.
Even after placing the wristband on me, she again asked me to spell my information. When I questioned why I had to keep repeating it, she said I was being rude and called security.
Two male security officers with dogs came over.
My 10-year-old son heard her call security, became frightened, and started crying. He was already dealing with the emotional stress of his younger brother having leukemia. This unnecessary escalation caused him additional distress and made the situation traumatic for him as well.
I had to call my husband, who had to leave our son alone in his hospital room after chemotherapy and come downstairs to help me. By then, both my older son and I were crying.
Later, I went back to the front desk and finally received a clear explanation: biological parents receive wristbands because they can participate in medical decisions, while other visitors receive Visitor stickers.
If someone had simply explained that from the beginning, there would have been no problem.
My frustration was never about wearing a wristband. It was about inconsistent procedures, poor communication, repeated questioning despite valid ID, and an unnecessary escalation to security in front of my children.
If parents are required to wear wristbands, then clearly post that policy and train all employees to follow it consistently. Parents should not be given a Visitor sticker one day and then treated suspiciously the next day for asking why the procedure changed.
I also felt singled out. I am an Asian woman, and I cannot ignore how uncomfortable and targeted this interaction made me feel. I cannot know what motivated the employees involved, but I was left with the strong impression that I was being unnecessarily pushed and intimidated.
Please review the footage from June 11 around 5:00 p.m. and speak with the employees who were working at the front desk and wristband station.
I am not asking for special treatment. I am asking for clear rules, consistency, compassion, and respectful communication.
Parents of seriously ill children are already living through a nightmare. Hospital staff should not make that nightmare worse.

I have trusted Phoenix Children’s with my kids for nearly 17 years, which is exactly why this experience was so disappointing.

I brought my son in because he needed minor medical attention that could not wait until morning, and Phoenix Children’s was the only nearby facility open. Based on our previous experiences with PCH, I didn’t think twice about bringing him there.

While we waited, our insurance information was taken. I specifically told the person collecting our information that I could not find the correct address in their system that matched the address on our insurance card. At no point were we told that our insurance was not accepted or that there was an issue processing it. Had we been told that, we could have made an informed decision about whether to continue with treatment or go elsewhere.

Instead, the first indication we had that there was a problem was when the bills started arriving. We are now receiving multiple bills totaling approximately $5,000 for this single visit, including separate facility, provider, and testing charges.

What makes this even more frustrating is the level of care involved. The visit consisted primarily of a roughly five-minute ultrasound and an extremely brief interaction with the provider. I also question why the ultrasound was performed before we had a meaningful evaluation by the provider to determine whether it was actually necessary.

Had we been able to use an urgent care that evening, the same type of visit likely would have cost us under $500. Instead, we are being charged thousands.

Since receiving the bills, I have called PCH multiple times trying to resolve this. Our account was supposedly “reviewed,” but from my experience, that amounted to postponing payment rather than actually investigating or addressing our concerns. Even more frustrating, when our insurance requested that PCH complete a single form so the claim could potentially be addressed, PCH billing refused to complete it.

My biggest issues are simple:

1. We provided our insurance information before treatment and specifically raised a concern about the information in their system, yet no one informed us that our insurance was not accepted.
2. We were not given the opportunity to make an informed financial decision before thousands of dollars in charges were incurred.
3. Testing was performed without what I felt was an adequate provider evaluation beforehand to determine whether it was necessary.
4. After the fact, we actively tried to work with both PCH and our insurance company, yet PCH would not even complete the requested form that could potentially help resolve the claim.

I understand that medical care costs money, and I am not asking to receive care for free. What I expect is transparency, reasonable communication, and some willingness to help when a billing issue arises.

After nearly 17 years of mostly positive experiences with Phoenix Children’s, this visit has significantly changed my opinion. Right now, it feels far more focused on collecting payment than helping a longtime patient family resolve a legitimate billing concern.

⭐ 1/5 — First Time Trying It & Probably My Last

This was my FIRST time ever trying Mr. Pickles, and unfortunately, this was a terrible first impression. I was actually excited to try this place, which makes the experience even more disappointing.

I ordered a whole Chicken Bacon Ranch on a Dutch Crunch roll, added pepperoni, bacon, and chicken breast, with ranch on the side, NO red onions and NO pickles. I also ordered a whole Reuben on marble rye with extra Swiss and Thousand Island on the side, plus individual macaroni salad and potato salad.

The receipt clearly shows my order and exactly how I requested everything, but there was NO ranch dressing for my Chicken Bacon Ranch and NO Thousand Island dressing for my Reuben. How do you send out a Chicken Bacon Ranch with no ranch and a Reuben with no Thousand Island, especially when the receipt specifically says both dressings were supposed to be on the side?

That completely ruined both sandwiches for me. I shouldn’t have to get home and realize that two of the main things that actually make these sandwiches what they are were left out.

And this wasn’t me forgetting to request them—the receipt is right there. “Ranch Dressing (on side)” and “Thousand Island (on side)” are both printed on the ticket. Someone simply did not check the order before it went out.

When you’re paying your money for food, you expect the restaurant to at least make sure everything you ordered is actually in the bag. Especially for a first-time customer. I wanted to try Mr. Pickles and see what the hype was about, but instead I ended up disappointed and feeling like I wasted my money.

Honestly, I wish I could get my money back. That’s how unhappy I am with this order. I paid for food I didn’t get to enjoy the way it was supposed to be served.

For a sandwich shop, getting the sandwiches and their basic condiments right should be the bare minimum. This was my first experience here, and unfortunately, it may very well be my last.

If you order from this location, check your entire bag before you leave. Check the sandwiches, check the sides, and definitely check for your dressings, because apparently having it clearly printed on the receipt doesn’t mean it’ll actually make it into your order.

one_star_reviews.text: Came to this location because the one i usually go to had no 7 passenger cars and im a gold member so usually i just get the keys and leave, well the guy here told me my drivers license is not good when i have rented cars at hertz for years. So they had me waiting for the manager forever with no AC here, this location is the horrible with customer service.

Extremely disappointing—and a serious safety concern

I rented a car from Hertz at Phoenix Sky Harbor through Expedia. When I arrived, my reserved vehicle was unavailable, so Hertz substituted an Infiniti. The vehicle was extremely dirty inside and out, and I was told to have it washed myself with the promise that I would be reimbursed.

The much more serious issue was the condition of the vehicle itself.

My husband, daughter, son-in-law, 12-year-old grandson, and I drove more than 100 miles from Phoenix to Flagstaff before my husband noticed that the left front tire was severely damaged, with a large gouge and significant portions of the tread torn away. I have photographs documenting the condition.

What is extremely concerning is that this damage was present when Hertz gave us the vehicle. We had unknowingly driven more than 100 miles on Arizona highways with our entire family in the car.

We immediately tried contacting Hertz but initially could not get through to anyone. The following day, we were instructed to take the vehicle to the Hertz location in Flagstaff.

The Flagstaff Hertz employees inspected the vehicle and agreed that it should never have been rented in that condition. Unfortunately, they had no replacement vehicle available, so we had to end the rental.

My biggest question is: How does a vehicle with a tire in this condition get inspected, approved, and handed to a customer in the first place?

A mechanical problem that develops during a rental is one thing. Giving a customer a vehicle with an existing, visibly damaged tire is something entirely different—especially when that customer is traveling with a family, including a child.

I want to give credit where it is due: the Flagstaff Hertz employees were professional and helpful, and Expedia ultimately worked with Hertz and obtained a full refund for me.

However, a full refund doesn’t change the fact that my family was placed in a potentially dangerous situation. Hertz needs to take a serious look at its vehicle inspection and safety procedures. No customer should have to discover a tire in this condition after driving more than 100 miles.

The staff at Hertz Phoenix Sky Harbor provided the most aggressive, manipulative, and unprofessionally rude service my wife and I have ever experienced.

The agent scoffed at me while sneaking unwanted insurance add-ons into a "basic" package. Another employee cynically tried to play on my wife's fears to force the upgrade, falsely claiming the car had no spare tire.

As someone who rents 5–6 cars a year, this branch is miles below Hertz standards. Do not rent a car at Hertz Phoenix Sky Harbor!
The "free" unsolicited upgrade wasn't free. They socked me on the insurance. Not going back.

Poor Customer Service
Hertz customer service told me that someone at the Phoenix Sky Harbor airport facility will get back to me… Ha.
Well, that hasn’t happened and the line either rings busy or there is no answer. The website indicates they’re open 24 hours but at 5 o’clock their recording goes on stating to call during normal business hours. I’m so disgusted with these people not getting back to me when there was an accident in inexcusable.

Disappointing Customer Service Experience at Hertz PHX Sky Harbor

I’m a Hertz President’s Circle member and rent from Hertz almost every month. I’ve generally continued choosing Hertz because of employer and my previous positive experiences in different states and the benefits that come with President’s Circle. Since I live in Arizona, I don’t normally need to rent a vehicle from the Phoenix Sky Harbor location, so today was one of my first experiences using President’s Circle at PHX.

Unfortunately, the customer service experience was surprisingly poor.

My fiancée and I went to the President’s Circle area to select our vehicle. Almost every vehicle available appeared to be an SUV. Toward the very end of the President’s Circle area, we noticed several sedans with license plates from different states. Since we preferred a sedan, I simply wanted to know whether those vehicles were also part of President’s Circle.

There was a Black gentleman wearing a Hertz shirt near those vehicles and getting into one of the cars. I politely asked him, “Is this President’s Circle too?”

Instead of simply answering the question or directing me to someone who could help, he gave me a blank, dismissive look and said, “No.”

I then politely asked what that lane/section was, and his response was, “This is my car.”

I wasn’t asking for his car. I wasn’t asking him to give me a vehicle or make an exception for me. I was simply asking a Hertz employee—or someone wearing a Hertz uniform—a basic question about where the President’s Circle area ended and what the neighboring lane was.

If he wasn’t the right person to ask, a simple “Sorry, I’m not sure” or “You’ll need to ask someone at the exit/customer service area” would have been perfectly fine. It was the dismissive attitude toward such a simple and polite question that bothered me.

We eventually selected an SUV from President’s Circle and proceeded to the exit. Unfortunately, the interaction there wasn’t much better.

The employee at the exit asked me for the mileage, which I provided. She then asked me to open the vehicle door. The door remained open for what felt like several minutes while we waited without any explanation. She later asked for my driver’s license, took it, and eventually returned it.

That was it.

There was no “Thank you,” “You’re all set,” “Have a good trip,” or even an indication that the process was finished and that I could close the door and leave. We were basically left sitting there wondering whether we were done.

I started my own career in customer service, so I understand that employees have difficult days and deal with hundreds of customers. I also don’t expect anyone to go above and beyond for every interaction. But basic acknowledgment, communication, and courtesy should be a minimum expectation—especially from a company like Hertz and at a major airport location such as Phoenix Sky Harbor.

I realize writing something like this can make someone sound overly demanding, but I genuinely wasn’t asking for special treatment because of my President’s Circle status. I was asking a simple question and later going through a routine exit process. A basic response, some direction, and a “thank you” would have completely changed the experience.

As someone who rents from Hertz frequently and has earned President’s Circle status, this experience was disappointing and very different from the level of service I would expect from Hertz.

My experience at this recovery center was very disappointing. I expected a structured, clinically focused program centered on sobriety and treatment for co-occurring mental health conditions. Instead, it often felt more like a retreat, with a heavy emphasis on sightseeing, group bonding, and arts and crafts, while practical recovery education, relapse prevention, and individualized therapy seemed to take a back seat.

I was also concerned by what I perceived as weak professional boundaries. In my experience, fraternization between clients was not adequately discouraged, and I observed physical contact and other interactions that I felt were inappropriate for a treatment setting. The music room has no cameras and people were using it to have relations...

I also had concerns about professionalism related to texting, taking pictures, and inconsistent enforcement of the dress code, including clients wearing bikinis during my stay.

People seeking treatment deserve a program that prioritizes evidence-based addiction care, strong clinical boundaries, and comprehensive mental health treatment. That was not my experience. If you're considering this facility, I recommend asking detailed questions about the clinical schedule, treatment for co-occurring disorders, staff boundaries, dress code enforcement, and policies regarding client interactions before making a decision.

The bad: After replacing both coils, we found trash and insulation tracked through the house. The air handler was left with a poor tape job that is leaking air into the attic. The insulation on the refrigerant line was not properly replaced. At the outdoor condenser, they left evidence of the leak and didn’t reinstall the caps on the refrigerant lines.

The worst: They did not provide an itemized bill. When we questioned why the final bill was at the very top of the estimate, we were initially told it was because they had added 3 lbs of refrigerant during the initial service call. They did not. The explanation then changed to the claim that they had to replace all of the refrigerant in the system.

That may be justified if the existing refrigerant was contaminated, but this was never communicated to us before the work was completed. At approximately $100/lb, replacing 10 lbs of refrigerant is not a minor expense. We were given no documentation showing that the existing refrigerant could not be recovered and reused.

When we questioned the charge, the explanation we eventually received was that the system had “high subcooling,” which they said was typically a sign of air or other non-condensables in the system. However, they provided none of the actual pressure or subcooling readings to support that diagnosis.

The fact that the bill landed at the very top of the quoted range, combined with the lack of an itemized invoice and changing explanations for the refrigerant charge, left us with the distinct impression that we were charged for materials that had not been adequately explained or documented.

Bottom line: The initial diagnostic service was good, but the installation quality, cleanup, communication, and especially the billing were unacceptable. Based on the information we were ultimately given, we believe we were overcharged by at least $500. I would strongly recommend getting a detailed, itemized quote and documenting exactly how much refrigerant is being recovered and added before allowing this company to perform the work.

I do not recommend Stanton Optical in Glendale. My main issue was how Haylee and store manager John Martinez handled a mistake made by their own store.

I brought my 14-year-old son in to get contacts and learn how to insert them. After two appointments, he was still having difficulty, so they sent him home with a trial pair to practice.

Afterward, I received TWO voicemails from the store saying his contacts were ready for pickup and telling me to come in at my earliest convenience. I drove roughly an hour round trip specifically because of those messages.

When I arrived, Haylee refused to give me the contacts because my son supposedly needed another insertion appointment. I showed Haylee the voicemail transcription on my phone and had her read it herself. It clearly said the contacts were ready for pickup and told me to come in at my earliest convenience. Instead of acknowledging their miscommunication, the situation became argumentative.

I asked for a refund. I paid approximately $400 in CASH, but they refused to return my cash and said I would have to wait up to 20 business days for a corporate check.

I still agreed to make another appointment for my son. About an hour before that appointment, store manager John Martinez called and told me he wanted me to apologize to Haylee before they would continue with the appointment. I refused. I don’t believe I owe an apology for being frustrated after their own voicemail caused me to make an unnecessary trip. John then hung up on me.

Now my 14-year-old son has no contacts, I’m out approximately $400, and I have to spend another $400 somewhere else while waiting up to 20 business days for my refund. This has put me in a financial difficulty that could have easily been avoided.

Mistakes happen. My problem is the lack of accountability and how Haylee and John Martinez handled the mistake afterward. A simple acknowledgment and apology would have resolved this.

Instead, they lost a customer and left me waiting for my money while my son still doesn’t have his contacts.

I absolutely would not recommend this location.

one_star_reviews.text:
Terrible customer service — especially from Pedro, who I believe is the owner or manager.
I originally opened a claim through Asurion, and because this is the closest location to my home, we have used this store before. Unfortunately, this is not our first frustrating experience with them.
The exact same issue with my phone happened about two months ago. I brought it into this location, they said they didn’t have my part so I had to reschedule and did, then I was told they fixed the issue, and now dealing with the SAME problem again. So when I had to come back this time, I was already frustrated because I was literally returning for the exact same issue I had previously brought to this store.
This time, someone from the store called me to set up an appointment. I explained that I couldn’t come in that same day, and the employee told me Saturday was fine. I specifically asked if I needed to make an appointment and was told NO. Based on what I was told BY THEIR STORE, I showed up Saturday expecting to have my phone taken care of.
Pedro’s response was essentially, “Nope, we have nothing for you. I don’t know what to tell you.” He told me I needed to call and file another claim because it wasn’t considered a warranty since they had never replaced the screen.
Rather than trying to help me resolve the situation, he was rude, dismissive, and showed absolutely no empathy for the fact that I was standing there with the exact same problem I had already brought to this store before.
I ended up calling AT&T while standing in the store, and Pedro continued insisting that the previous repair never happened. At that point, I was frustrated and did speak over him because I was trying to explain that THIS WAS THE SAME PROBLEM I HAD ALREADY DEALT WITH AT THIS STORE. I’ll own that I had an attitude at that point, but his rude and dismissive behavior is what got the situation there in the first place.
What makes it even worse is that, at the end of the conversation, AT&T confirmed that the store was the one that cancelled the appointment and documented that I didn’t want to schedule it. That is NOT what happened. I was told by the store employee that Saturday was fine and that I did not need to make an appointment. Somehow, that became me refusing to schedule.
Mistakes happen. I completely understand that. What I DON’T understand is having a customer come back for the exact same unresolved issue, being given incorrect information by your own store, and then being treated like an inconvenience when you show up.
The biggest issue for me was not even the inconvenience, it was Pedro’s attitude. There was no attempt to understand the situation, no empathy, and very little effort to actually help. Instead, I was met with rudeness and essentially told it was my problem to figure out.
I will say that the employee who ultimately came out and brought my phone back to me was very kind and respectful, and I appreciate that. Unfortunately, the experience with Pedro completely overshadowed that.
I would NOT recommend this location. If you are going to have customers return for the same issue, the absolute least you can do is treat them with respect and actually try to help resolve the situation especially when the confusion surrounding the appointment was caused by your own store.
